title.value: Radiomics-Based Machine Learning for Outcome Prediction in a Multicenter Phase II Study of Programmed Death-Ligand 1 Inhibition Immunotherapy for Glioblastoma
title.justification: The title directly reflects the study's focus on using machine learning to predict outcomes in glioblastoma treatment.
title.quote: Radiomics-Based Machine Learning for Outcome Prediction in a Multicenter Phase II Study of Programmed Death-Ligand 1 Inhibition Immunotherapy for Glioblastoma

extractions.description: This paper investigates the use of radiomics-based machine learning to predict outcomes in glioblastoma patients undergoing PD-L1 inhibition immunotherapy, using data from a multicenter trial. It focuses on the predictive value of MRI features at different treatment stages, highlighting the potential for machine learning to assess patient survival and progression.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on medical outcomes for glioblastoma patients rather than on ecological or climate-related sustainability topics.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our purpose was to determine whether MR imaging radiomics-based machine learning can predict progression-free survival and overall survival in patients with glioblastoma on programmed death-ligand 1 inhibition immunotherapy.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not address climate or ecological sustainability themes; it is focused on medical research for glioblastoma treatment outcomes.
primary_category.quote: Our purpose was to determine whether MR imaging radiomics-based machine learning can predict progression-free survival and overall survival in patients with glioblastoma on programmed death-ligand 1 inhibition immunotherapy.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary aspects of climate or ecological sustainability addressed in this paper.
secondary_categories.quote: Our study identified texture features from all conventional imaging sequences for both enhancing and WT volume contributory to predicting survival from first on-treatment MR imaging.
